summary: AWS Cost Explorer experienced a reported multi-hour interruption after an engineering change associated in press reporting with Amazon's Kiro coding tool; Amazon disputes autonomous-AI causation and attributes the event to human error and misconfigured access controls.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The Financial Times reported an approximately 13-hour Cost Explorer interruption and linked the triggering change to use of Kiro. Amazon later described the event as a brief interruption of one service in one region caused by a user error and access-control configuration, not autonomous AI action; it reported no customer inquiries and no impact to compute, storage, databases or AI services.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: A bounded AWS service outage occurred, but the available public accounts conflict about whether Kiro had a causal role. VIGIL therefore assesses the materialised service consequence separately from the disputed mechanism and leaves taxonomy classification unresolved.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case illustrates why AI attribution in software operations must be based on the actual change-authority and review chain rather than a tool's presence in an engineering workflow.
assessment_boundaries: Amazon expressly disputes that an autonomous AI action caused the interruption.
Public sources disagree on the duration and framing; no full technical postmortem is available.
